To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the cDNA encoding HSA was identified and characterized, (ii) HSA is expressed exclusively in hematopoetic tissues, (iii) three HSA genes were cloned and sequenced, and (iv) the HSA gene is expressed as an intron‐contained transcript and not as an intronless transcript.

the gene encoding the murine differentiation marker heat‐stable antigen is expressed exclusively in hematopoiesis, that the antigenic epitope recognized by anti‐heat‐stable antigen antibodies is proteinaceous, and that the gene is encoded by an intron‐contained gene which is expressed in all tissues examined and an intronless gene which may code for a transmembrane form of the protein.
we have isolated a mouse cDNA encoding the heat‐stable hematopoietic antigen and that the antigenic determinants recognized by anti‐heat‐stable antibodies are proteinaceous.

the molecular characterization of a differentiation antigen of mouse pre‐B cells.
the molecular cloning of a gene for an important hematopoietic cell marker.
the molecular cloning and characterization of a mouse cDNA encoding the heat‐stable hematopoietic antigen.

the HSA gene family consists of at least three genes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have isolated the gene for the murine HSA differentiation marker, which is expressed in a restricted set of tissues.
the murine HSA is a protein‐encoded cell surface molecule which is expressed by all lymphoid cells except plasma cells and is encoded by a single gene.
the HSA gene family is comprised of at least three genes: one of these genes encodes a protein with a transmembranal domain and a cytosolic tail, and two of these genes are retroposons.
